name: b02-ip-offset
title: Why the BMC needs an IP offset
spec: Two horizontal rows of address boxes sharing one network, 10.141.0.0/16. Top row labelled boot interface (BOOTIF) with ten small boxes 10.141.0.1 to 10.141.0.10. Bottom row labelled bmc interface with offset 0.0.0.20 with ten small boxes 10.141.0.21 to 10.141.0.30. A green bracket or gap between the two rows, with the note: the offset moves the BMC sequence along the block so no address is claimed twice. Beside the first row a grey note: without the offset, both sequences start at .1 and collide on every address. Orange highlight on the gap between the two rows. Monospace for the addresses and the offset value.
alt: Boot and BMC address ranges with an offset
cap: IP offset: the BMC addresses start after the boot addresses, so the two interfaces never share an address.

name: b02-burn-split
title: How a burn run uses the pre-install and post-install phases
spec: A left-to-right flow of four steps with number circles 1 to 4 and arrows between them. Step 1: burn --config <name> -n node001..node064 start, reboot the node into the node-installer environment (RAM-based). Step 2: run every pre-install phase, destructive block-level disk and memory tests allowed, local drives not mounted as a root filesystem. Step 3: all pre-install phases pass, provision the full software image onto disk and boot the production kernel. Step 4: run every post-install phase with full driver support, examples hpl, GPU DCGM stress tests, InfiniBand bandwidth checks. Above step 4, a side container labelled stress phase with two parallel boxes: a timed stress test (hpl or memtester) and, beside it, a monitor marked endless equals 1 (mce_check, kmon), with the note: monitors stop when the last non-endless test in the phase finishes. Orange note on step 2: destructive tests are safe here because no running OS is on the drives.
anchor: ### 10.2 Designing a production burn-in gate with `burnconfigs`
alt: The pre-install and post-install burn phases
cap: Burn-in order: destructive tests run in the RAM-based installer before the image is provisioned, then full-stack tests run on the production kernel.
